name: Hanoi
summary: You wake up to Turtle Tower in Hoan Kiem and the lanes north of the lake. Stay if that walk, a lunch bowl, and one morning in Ba Dinh are the trip. Go on to Ninh Binh, Ha Long, or Sapa if the city is only where the plane landed. The Old Quarter is a separate walk. Use the link. This page does not repeat it.
fee: The lake path is free. Sight tickets are separate.
getThere: Noi Bai is 28 km north, or about 27 km. By car about 45–60 minutes, or about 40.
bestMonths: April to June or September to December
seoTitle: Hanoi travel guide: the lake, the citadel, and what to eat
seoDescription: Noi Bai is 28 km north of the city, or about 27 km on the airline and Grab pages. April to June, or September to December, is the easier window.
intro: You come for the lake. Turtle Tower sits in Hoan Kiem, and the lanes north of it are where the morning starts, with pho before the courtyards fill. Stay if that walk is the trip. Go on to Ninh Binh, Ha Long, or Sapa if the north outside the city is the trip.

Ba Dinh is a different morning: the citadel, the mausoleum, and One Pillar Pagoda, and they are not one ticket. After dark the corner Vietnam Tourism names is Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen. The Old Quarter is a separate walk. Use the link. This page does not repeat it.
gettingAround: Noi Bai is 28 km north of Ha Noi on the airport’s aeronautical page, and about 27 km from the center on Vietnam Airlines and on Grab. A car is about 45 to 60 minutes on the airline page, and about 40 minutes on Grab. Bus 86 to Ha Noi Railway Station is 50,000 VND, departing 7:00 to 22:15. Vietnam Airlines lists an express bus at 45,000 VND. Both fares stay.

Inside the lake grid, walk. Metro Line 2A and Line 3 both list 5:30 to 22:00. Line 3 stops at Van Mieu, for the Temple of Literature, and at Ha Noi Station. The walk from the station to the temple gate is check on arrival. A ride from the lake to Ba Dinh or West Lake is check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: North of the lake
stayAreas.summary: The lanes above Hoan Kiem. You can walk to the shore and to the morning pho streets. The streets are noisy late, and Ta Hien is the evening corner.

stayAreas.name: South of Hoan Kiem
stayAreas.summary: Quieter streets around the Opera House. Still a walk to the lake. The history museum and Trang Tien sit on this side.

eat: Start the day with pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes, including Hang Vai. At lunch, bun cha is the bowl, almost only at lunch, around Cua Dong. In the afternoon, egg coffee is the sit-down cup in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley.
Vietnam Tourism names shops on those streets. This page does not rank them. Banh mi is not on that Hanoi dish list, so it is not given a Hanoi line here.
interestsBody: Come for the lake walk, a morning in Ba Dinh, and the bowls Vietnam Tourism ties to this city: pho, bun cha, and egg coffee. The Old Quarter is a separate walk through the grid north of the lake. Use the link. This page does not repeat it.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Pho in the morning, bun cha at lunch, and egg coffee in the afternoon. The lanes are Hang Vai, Cua Dong, and the Nguyen Huu Huan alley.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Pho in the morning, bun cha at lunch, and egg coffee when you sit down. The plate photos are the bowls, not a shop list.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Silk and silver in the Old Quarter lanes, wholesale goods at Dong Xuan, and a shopping center on Hai Bà Trưng.

blocks.heading: The lanes and Dong Xuan
paragraphs: The Old Quarter sits on land that was once a cluster of artisan streets outside the citadel. Shop signs still hint at silver, silk, and herbal medicine, even where the ground floors now sell luggage and cafe seats. Walk it in the morning, before the pavements fill.

Dong Xuan is the quarter’s main covered market. The district page calls it useful for a look at wholesale goods more than for souvenirs, and it says entry is free. No hour is printed there. The hours are check on arrival. Stall prices are check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Tràng Tiền Plaza
paragraphs: Tràng Tiền Plaza’s own site calls the building a shopping center. A page on that site dated 16 May 2026 prints the address 24 Hai Bà Trưng, Cửa Nam ward, and the hours Monday to Thursday 09:30 to 21:30, Friday to Sunday 09:30 to 22:00. No door fee is printed. Entry is check on arrival.

cards.title: Dong Xuan Market
cards.summary: The covered market in the Old Quarter. Wholesale goods more than souvenirs, and entry is free, on the district page. The hours are check on arrival.

cards.title: Tràng Tiền Plaza
cards.summary: The shopping center at 24 Hai Bà Trưng. The mall’s 16 May 2026 page prints 09:30 to 21:30 Monday to Thursday, and 09:30 to 22:00 Friday to Sunday. No door fee is printed.

interestGroups.title: The lake and the lanes
interestGroups.summary: Hoan Kiem is the landmark. The lanes north of it are a separate walk, on the link. The cathedral and the water-puppet theatre sit on this walk.

cards.title: Hoan Kiem Lake
cards.summary: The lake path is free and open all day. Turtle Tower stands in the water. The temple on the island is a separate ticket.

cards.title: Ngoc Son Temple
cards.summary: The The Huc bridge and the temple on the island. Adult 50,000 VND. The two hour tables do not match.

cards.title: Old Quarter
cards.summary: The grid of lanes north of the lake, walked separately. Use the link. This page does not repeat it.

interestGroups.title: Ba Dinh
interestGroups.summary: The citadel, the mausoleum, and One Pillar Pagoda are three gates, not one ticket.

cards.title: Imperial Citadel
cards.summary: UNESCO, 2010. Adult 100,000 VND from 1 January 2025. Open 8:00 to 17:00 every day.

cards.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
cards.summary: Morning visits on set days. The official FAQ says free. Vietnam Tourism prints 40,000 VND.

cards.title: One Pillar Pagoda
cards.summary: The wooden pagoda on one pillar. 25,000 VND. The hours and the emperor’s name differ by source.

interestGroups.title: Temple of Literature
interestGroups.summary: The Confucian temple west of the old commercial streets. Daytime ticket 70,000 VND. The night price is not one number.

cards.title: Temple of Literature
cards.summary: Operator hours 8:00 to 17:00 every day. Vietnam Tourism prints a different daytime window and a 199,000 VND night tour.

interestGroups.title: West Lake
interestGroups.summary: The large lake in Tay Ho. A shore fee was not published. Tran Quoc is the pagoda on the water.

cards.title: West Lake
cards.summary: The shore north of the center. The fee and the minutes from Hoan Kiem are check on arrival.

cards.title: Tran Quoc Pagoda
cards.summary: The stupa on the West Lake shore. The fee and the hours are check on arrival.

faqs.q: How do you get into the city from Noi Bai?
faqs.a: The airport page puts Noi Bai 28 km north of Ha Noi. Vietnam Airlines and Grab say about 27 km. A car is about 45 to 60 minutes on the airline page, and about 40 minutes on Grab. Bus 86 to Ha Noi Railway Station is 50,000 VND, from 7:00 to 22:15. Vietnam Airlines lists an express bus at 45,000 VND.

faqs.q: When can you visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum?
faqs.a: The operator opens mornings on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, and closes Monday and Friday except 19 May, 2 September, and the first day of Tet when those fall on a closed day. The government portal also closes it from 4 September 2026 to 2 November 2026. The official FAQ says the visit is free. Vietnam Tourism prints 40,000 VND.

season.label: April to June, or September to December
season.note: Vietnam Tourism calls April to June, or September to December, the easier window. June to August is hot, humid, and rainy. Late December to March can fall to about 10°C. September to November sits around 25°C, and April can pass 30°C. Tet moves on the lunar calendar. In the days before it, seats sell out, and the first days of the city are quieter.
